LESSON: HUMAN REPRODUCTIVE SYSTEM

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Living Things and their Environment
Topic 3.1: Human Reproductive System

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Human Reproductive System. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What are the physical, social, and emotional changes that take place during adolescence?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify parts of the male and female reproductive systems
2. describe functions of parts of the male and female reproductive system
3. describe the physical changes that take place in boys and girls during adolescence

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: HUMAN REPRODUCTIVE SYSTEM
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Human Reproductive System helps you succeed in INTEGRATED SCIENCE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: HUMAN REPRODUCTIVE SYSTEM
Study Human Reproductive System like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify parts of the male and female reproductive systems

What this means
In this part you learn to identify parts of the male and female reproductive systems. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify parts of the male and female reproductive systems.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Human Reproductive System” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify parts of the male and female reproductive systems. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe functions of parts of the male and female reproductive system

What this means
In this part you learn to describe functions of parts of the male and female reproductive system. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe functions of parts of the male and female reproductive system.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Human Reproductive System matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe functions of parts of the male and female reproductive system. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Describe the physical changes that take place in boys and girls during adolescence

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the physical changes that take place in boys and girls during adolescence. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the physical changes that take place in boys and girls during adolescence.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Human Reproductive System this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the physical changes that take place in boys and girls during adolescence. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Human Reproductive System is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Human Reproductive System” around your school. (skill: identify parts of the male and female reproductive systems)

Example 2: Say why Human Reproductive System matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: describe functions of parts of the male and female reproductive system)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Human Reproductive System this week. (skill: describe the physical changes that take place in boys and girls during adolescence)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Human Reproductive System to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify parts of the male and female reproductive systems.
3. Practise this skill: describe functions of parts of the male and female reproductive system.
4. Practise this skill: describe the physical changes that take place in boys and girls during adolescence.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Human Reproductive System from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Human Reproductive System: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Human Reproductive System?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are the physical, social, and emotional changes that take place during adolescence?
2. How are developmental changes managed during adolescence?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Human Reproductive System means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify parts of the male and female reproductive systems.
5. Be able to: describe functions of parts of the male and female reproductive system.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
